_note: UK figures for the 2026/27 tax year used by the dividend, salary vs dividends, contractor, capital gains, inheritance tax, statutory pay, redundancy, holiday and pension calculators (tools/build-uk-calcs.js). Income tax bands, the personal allowance and employee National Insurance are NOT here: they are read from data/tax/gb/gb.2026-27.json so the two can't disagree. Every figure below was read from the GOV.UK page given in its source on lastChecked; the monthly check confirms them.

dividends.note: 'This table shows the rates from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027': 10.75%, 35.75%, 39.35%; dividend allowance £500 (2025/26: 8.75%, 33.75%, 39.35%).

corporationTax.note: Financial year from 1 April 2026: small profits rate 19% (profits under £50,000), main rate 25% (over £250,000), marginal relief limits £50,000 and £250,000, standard fraction 3/200.

employerNI.note: Secondary threshold £5,000 a year, category A employer rate 15%, Employment Allowance £10,500. Not available where a company's only employee paid above the secondary threshold is its sole director (https://www.gov.uk/claim-employment-allowance/eligibility).

capitalGains.note: 18% within the basic rate band and 24% above it on gains from 6 April 2026; Business Asset Disposal Relief 18% from 6 April 2026; tax-free allowance £3,000 for 2026 to 2027 (https://www.gov.uk/capital-gains-tax/allowances).

inheritanceTax.note: £325,000 threshold, which 'can increase to £500,000' when a home goes to direct descendants (so a £175,000 residence nil-rate band); 40%, or 36% with 10% or more to charity; the residence band reduces by £1 for every £2 over the £2 million taper threshold (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/inheritance-tax-residence-nil-rate-band); unused threshold transfers to a spouse or civil partner.

statutoryPay.note: SMP: 90% of average weekly earnings for the first 6 weeks, then £194.32 or 90% (whichever is lower) for the next 33 weeks; up to 39 weeks; eligibility: average at least £129 a week (https://www.gov.uk/maternity-pay-leave/eligibility). Paternity pay £194.32 or 90% (https://www.gov.uk/paternity-pay-leave/pay).

redundancy.note: Half a week's pay for each full year under 22, one week for each full year 22 to 40, one and a half weeks for each full year 41 or older; weekly pay capped at £751, service at 20 years, maximum £22,530, for redundancies on or after 6 April 2026; 2 years' service needed.

holiday.note: 5.6 weeks' paid holiday a year, limited to 28 days; irregular-hours and part-year workers accrue 12.07% of hours worked in each pay period (leave years starting from 1 April 2024).

pensions.note: Usually up to 25% tax-free, at most £268,275; full new State Pension £241.30 a week (https://www.gov.uk/new-state-pension/what-youll-get).

landlords.note: Finance costs get a tax reduction at the basic rate, 'currently 20%'.
